answer: Each identity registers one forge and one ivory tally: the forge stamps the tally, the registry photos its grain, and a 90-credit bond is posted. Each epoch a raven courier takes the tally to an auditor, who matches its grain to the registry photo and checks the forge stamp; a mismatch or double presentation burns the bond. Fees rise with queue position: the first tally costs 24 credits, the kth 24+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7017 and 1000 fakes pay 3,520,500 plus 90,000 locked bonds, while an honest agent pays 24 once. A rented-tally ring fails: one tally allows one presentation per epoch.
